blocks.content: Course: Make Your Website Interactive with JavaScript
Key Patterns You Used
At the start of this course, the portfolio looked complete. It had structure. It had styling. But it didn't respond.
Now it does.
Across the entire project, the same small set of patterns kept showing up. Not because the features were the same, but because the thinking behind them was.
Connecting JavaScript
You connected JavaScript to the page using a script tag. From there, clicks and scroll events made elements respond.
Selecting and Updating the Page
You selected elements using querySelector. Then updated text, attributes, or classes to change what appeared on the screen.
Toggling Classes
Instead of changing styles directly, you added or removed classes. CSS handled the appearance. JavaScript controlled which state was active.
Scroll and Conditions
You listened for scroll events, checked scrollY, compared it to a number, and triggered changes like a sticky header.
State
You used a variable as the source of truth. When that value changed, the interface updated to match it. That's how the slider and button boundaries worked.
Modals and Forms
You opened and closed modals with clean functions. You read form values, validated input, prevented reload, and showed feedback.
Different features. Same pattern underneath.
Change the state. Update the UI.
Next, there's one quick question to reinforce the core idea before moving into the final challenges.
How does it work?
